newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf French strike extended to Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Elf French strike extended to Wednesday.

text.p: Elf Aquitaine workers extended a six-day-old French refinery strike on Tuesday evening, pledging to keep up their protest over job cuts until at least Wednesday morning, officials from France's main trade union said.
Workers who arrive for new shifts at Elf's three French plants on Wednesday are then likely to extend the action again, possibly until Thursday, the officials from the CFDT union said.

"We are probably going to keep going until at least Thursday because we have obtained nothing," said a union representative at one of the plants involved in the strike, the Grandpuits refinery near Paris.
Workers at two other plants, Feyzin near Lyon and Donges in western France, the country's biggest refinery, have opted to stay out until Wednesday lunchtime, union officials there said.
The strike was being renewed at shift changes, they said.

Unions said they were dissatisfied with Elf proposals to hold negotiations over pay and working conditions on Thursday, saying this was merely an earlier version of routine salary talks already scheduled for December 20.
The CFDT said in a statement earlier that the talks' agenda avoided the strikers' real demands that a plan to cut 10 percent of Elf's French refinery workforce should be scrapped.
Elf says the roughly 300 job reductions are needed to help its Elf Antar refining subsidiary improve its performance.
The strike has paralysed all Elf's refineries in France, reducing French refining capacity by a quarter and helping to drive up gasoline prices on both sides of the Atlantic.
